desc: Ideation: derive key identity K[i] = P[i] * inv(10^i) mod m; substring(i..j) divisible iff K[i]==K[j+1]; per-digit rules for d in 0..9
Implement sweep with prefix-mod counters for m in {3,7,9}; 10≡1 mod 3 and mod 9 so K = prefix mod directly; for m=7 maintain invPow (×5 each step), K = P7 * invPow % 7
Per j, branch on d = s[j]: '0'→0; '1','2','5'→j+1; '3','9'→counter3/9 lookup; '6'→counter3 lookup; '7'→counter7 lookup; '4'→two-digit rule; '8'→three-digit rule with fallbacks
Update order: compute K[j+1] per modulus, query relevant counter, then add all three K[j+1] values to counters

Brute-force O(n²) cross-check: all three examples (11, 18, 25) plus edge cases ("0"→0, "10"→1, "100"→1, "24"→3, "88"→3, "888"→6, "36"→3, "126"→5, "08"→2, "008"→3, "1000004"→7, etc.) and extensive random/exhaustive small-string testing — all matched
Edge-case verification for '8' (j=0, j=1, 3-digit fail with 2-digit fallback) and '4' (j=0); performance confirmed O(n), <0.1s at n=1e5
